claim: American Airlines is re-banking DFW from 9 departure banks to 13 in April 2026, dropping the 9am peak from about 110 to about 52 departures and pushing 40+ flights into currently underused hours (11am, 1pm, 3pm, 5pm, 9pm).
source_title: American Shifts for Smoother Schedules at DFW
supporting_excerpt: 9 departure banks (5am-11pm); Peak hour: 110 departures at 9am ... 13 departure banks across same timeframe; Peak hour: 52 departures (9am slot); Previously underutilized hours (11am, 1pm, 3pm, 5pm, 9pm) will each see 40+ flights
units: departures per hour, number of banks
caveat: PaxEx summarizes AA's public disclosure; the exact per-hour distribution may shift before April 2026.

claim: American is adding an average of 6 minutes of block time across 145 markets (CLT +17, DCA +10, MIA +9) alongside the DFW re-bank, explicitly to improve on-time and bag connect performance.
source_title: American Shifts for Smoother Schedules at DFW
supporting_excerpt: a bold and unprecedented investment in block time affecting 145 markets with average increases of 6 minutes (Charlotte +17 minutes, DCA +10 minutes, Miami +9 minutes)
caveat: Block-time additions signal AA's own read on ground-connectivity risk; secondary reporting.

claim: American operates roughly 930 peak-day departures and about 100,000 daily connecting customers at DFW.
source_title: Doubling down on DFW: American further strengthens its Flagship hub
supporting_excerpt: hub handles over 930 departures on peak days with connections for roughly 100,000 daily customers
units: departures per peak day; connecting customers per day

claim: Terminal F Phase 1 uses six prefabricated modules; the largest measured 278 feet long by 136 feet wide and weighed 3,320 tons, moved along an airside taxiway during a two-week overnight window in August 2026.
source_title: Dallas Fort Worth Airport completes record-breaking modular move as new terminal f construction reaches major milestone
supporting_excerpt: largest module stretched 278 feet long by 136 feet wide and weighed 3,320 tons, about the weight of 12 Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners
caveat: Individual module dimensions vary; largest cited.

claim: Terminal F Phase 1 is a 400,000-square-foot, 15-gate concourse; the associated Terminal E expansion adds more than 100,000 square feet of check-in, security, and baggage-claim facilities dedicated to Terminal F customers.
supporting_excerpt: 15 gates within a 400,000-square-foot concourse ... more than 100,000 square feet of new check-in, security and baggage claim facilities dedicated to customers flying in and out of Terminal F
denominator: Phase 1 only; full program is 31 gates
caveat: Widebody/narrowbody split, FIS/CBP configuration, and lounge SF not disclosed on the public page.

claim: Terminal F is being delivered by the Innovation Next+ joint venture (Archer Western, Turner, Phillips May, H. J. Russell, CARCON) with PGAL, Gensler, and Muller2 as designers.
source_title: Innovation Next+ Achieves Landmark Modular Delivery for DFW Terminal F Expansion
supporting_excerpt: design-build team for the first phase of Terminal F is Innovation Next+, a joint venture comprised of Archer Western Construction, Turner Construction Company, Phillips May Corporation, H. J. Russell & Company and CARCON Industries, with PGAL, Gensler and Muller2 as design team members
caveat: Team composition current as of Phase 1; may evolve for later phases.

claim: American's DFW premium package announced in 2026 includes a first-ever DFW Flagship Check-In near D30, a 37,000-square-foot Admirals Club in Terminal C (its largest in the network), and only a scaled-down Provisions by Admirals Club concept in Terminal F.
source_title: American Airlines to build 37,000-square-foot Admirals Club at DFW Airport
supporting_excerpt: new 37,000-square-foot Admirals Club lounge in Terminal C ... Flagship check-in facility in Terminal D near the D30 security checkpoint ... a quick-service 'Provisions by Admirals Club' concept in the future Terminal F
caveat: Provisions by Admirals Club is a scaled offering, not a Flagship-tier lounge; may or may not be a placeholder.

claim: The existing DFW Flagship Lounge (Terminal D) is approximately 23,000 square feet; the new Terminal C Admirals Club at 37,000 sf is roughly 60% larger.
source_title: American Airlines Launches New Premium Travel Facilities at Dallas Fort Worth Airport
supporting_excerpt: the Flagship Lounge in Terminal D spans approximately 23,000 square feet, making the new Admirals Club roughly 60% larger
caveat: Secondary source; Flagship Lounge Terminal D SF not confirmed by primary AA disclosure reviewed.

claim: Skylink is out of service every night from approximately 22:00 to 06:00 for maintenance, with only one loop operating in a single direction during that window; scheduled inter-terminal transit times rise to ~15 minutes when the second loop is down.
source_title: Skylink Maintenance FAQs | DFW International Airport
supporting_excerpt: Skylink maintenance routinely occurs overnight from 2200–0600, during which only one loop operates in a single direction, which can increase transit times between terminals to approximately 15 minutes
caveat: Standard operating condition, not an outage; airport confirms via official FAQ.

claim: A late-January 2023 winter storm produced a ground stop, 4-hour average delays after the stop was lifted, more than 1,100 cancellations on the peak day and 600+ additional cancellations the following day at DFW.
source_title: Winter storm prompts ground stop at DFW Airport
supporting_excerpt: ground stop was issued for all incoming aircraft ... average flight delays exceeding four hours ... more than 600 cancellations and more than 500 delays ... more than 1,100 cancellations on Monday
caveat: Local reporting; AA's own operational-impact figures were larger for network-wide effects.

claim: ACRP Synthesis 20 documents that terminal activation problems repeatedly trace back to airport operations staff being brought into design, construction, and commissioning too late, and recommends structured operator engagement across the full delivery cycle.
source_title: ACRP Synthesis 20: Airport Terminal Facility Activation Techniques
page_or_section: Summary and Chapter Six (Terminal Activation Policies)
supporting_excerpt: The synthesis recommends exploring ways of keeping airport operations staff engaged throughout the entire delivery process (planning, design, construction, commissioning, and activation).
caveat: Older synthesis, but the finding on operator engagement is the reference in the field.

claim: FAA AC 150/5300-13B is the governing federal design standard for airfield geometry including gate/apron dimensions keyed to Aircraft Design Group (ADG); Group V covers 777/787, Group VI covers 747-8/A380.
source_title: AC 150/5300-13B, Airport Design (with Change 1 and errata)
supporting_excerpt: FAA recommends using the standards and guidelines in this AC for application at civil airports
caveat: Guidance, not regulation, but federally funded projects treat it as binding.

claim: Industry practice cites passenger boarding bridge service life of approximately 20-25 years, with mid-life overhauls (canopies, motors, hydraulic cylinders, weather seals) typically required at 10-12 years.
source_title: Passenger Boarding Bridge (PBB) Maintenance: Preventing Delays at the Gate
supporting_excerpt: typical PBB service life is 20-25 years ... life expectancy is generally 10-12 years ... before some major maintenance will need to be performed, including replacing canopies, motors, hydraulic cylinders, and weather seals
caveat: Vendor-adjacent publication; operator experience varies with utilization and climate.

claim: World-class airport operations target 95%+ asset availability for critical systems including baggage handling, HVAC, and airfield lighting; MTBF is a core KPI in operator maintenance dashboards.
source_title: Essential Maintenance KPIs Every Airport Should Track
supporting_excerpt: World-class airport operations target 95% or higher asset availability for critical systems

claim: IATA CUPPS is the open technical standard that allows multiple airlines to share physical gate/check-in positions with common hardware and swappable airline application layers.
source_title: IATA Common Use Passenger Processing Systems (CUPPS) Technical Specifications
supporting_excerpt: CUPPS ... enables multiple airlines, service providers, or other users to share physical locations such as check-in desks, bag drops, gate positions ... based on an open standards-based environment
caveat: Standard; adoption is airport/carrier-specific and requires operator investment in shared IT.

claim: ACRP Report 139 codifies retrocommissioning of airport buildings as a whole-systems discipline, recognizing that terminal MEP systems drift from design intent within the first years of operation.
source_title: ACRP Report 139: Optimizing Airport Building Operations and Maintenance Through Retrocommissioning
supporting_excerpt: Optimizing Airport Building Operations and Maintenance Through Retrocommissioning: A Whole-Systems Approach
caveat: Retrocommissioning is a known post-handoff mitigation; not a substitute for commissioning done right the first time.

claim: DFW's joint press release on Terminal F names the amenity program (state-of-the-art amenities, expanded shops and restaurants, public art, a new centralized Skylink Station, walking connection to Terminal D, expanded parking with built-in curbside circulation, dedicated ticketing/check-in/security/baggage areas) but does not commit to a Flagship-tier lounge or a specific widebody gate count.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon (compiled from DFW/AA joint announcement)
supporting_excerpt: Named amenities in the joint announcement: state-of-the-art amenities; expanded shops and restaurants; public art installations; a new centralized Skylink Station; a walking connection to Terminal D; expanded parking garage designed with built-in curbside circulation; dedicated areas for ticketing, check-in, security screening, and baggage claim.
caveat: Context packet compiled by the run; the underlying source is the joint press release paraphrased.

claim: American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers in 2025 (70.8M of 85.7M) and 82% of departures, making the AA/DFW operating interface effectively a single-tenant relationship even outside Terminal F.
source_title: Airport Context Packet — DFW Terminal F, 2043 Horizon
supporting_excerpt: American Airlines carried 82.6% of DFW's passengers (70.8 million of 85.7 million) and operated 82% of departures
units: percent of passengers, percent of departures
caveat: Secondary sources cited in context packet; DFW official CY2025 statistics pending confirmation.
